item.title: THE LONG EXHALE | A GROUP EXHIBITION — Fri Aug 28, 5:00 PM — 5 Points Gallery
item.description:
5 Points Gallery is pleased to present The Long Exhale, bringing together work by the ten artists of 5 Points Gallery. As the pace of summer begins to soften, The Long Exhale invites visitors to pause, look closely, and linger. The exhibition offers a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist offering a distinct creative perspective. Join us for the Opening Reception on Friday, August 21, 2026, from 6–9 pm to meet the artists. The exhibition runs from August 20 through September 12, 2026. Visit 5 Points Gallery in person or online at https://5pointsgallery.com. All work from the exhibition is available for shipping or pickup. Gallery hours: Thursdays and Fridays 5–9pm and Saturdays 1–9pm. Artists are available to talk about their work. For a private viewing, contact us at info@5pointsgallery.com.

item.title: CDVS Workshop: Effective Data Visualization — Mon Aug 31, 6:00 PM — Online
item.description:
Visualization is a powerful way to reveal patterns in data, attract attention, and get your message across to an audience quickly and clearly. But, there are many steps in that journey from exploration to information to influence, and many choices to make when putting it all together to tell your story. I will cover some basic guidelines for effective visualization, point out a few common pitfalls to avoid, and run through a critique and iterations of an existing visualization to help you start seeing better choices beyond the software defaults. This event is open to non-Duke participants.

item.title: 2026-2027 Ignite Makers Program Begins — Tue Sep 1 — None
item.description:
The Ignite Makers Program is a free program that runs from September through April each year for high school students. This program challenges students to use Human-Centered and Engineering Design processes to research problems related to the UN Global Goals of Clean Energy (Light Team), Clean Water (Water Team), or Good Health (Health Team).
Students meet weekly with their Duke undergraduate mentors both via Zoom and at Duke to identify a problem, brainstorm a solution, prototype designs, and test solutions. Each year, Makers present their final projects at "Duke Day," a Science Fair-style Conference on Duke University's campus. Examples of previous Makers' prototypes can be found on our website: https://www.gwht-ignite-learning.com/makers-program
Official program dates will be shared with selected applicants.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Botany Spotlight: Amazing Plant Adaptations to Terrestrial Environments — Tue Sep 1, 10:00 AM — Sarah P. Duke Gardens
item.description:
Plants thrive in an extraordinary diversity of habitats, from hot, dry deserts to humid tropical rain forests to cold arctic tundra to expansive grasslands. But unlike most animals (including humans), plants are constrained to live in a fixed location. They can't move to find the water, sunlight and nutrients they need to survive, and they can't migrate to avoid changing or harsh environmental conditions. The varied ways plants have evolved and adapted to overcome these challenges are truly amazing. Join Alec Motten, professor emeritus, Duke University Department of Biology, for a lively exploration of how plants respond to and shape their environment. You'll start with an in-depth overview in the classroom before venturing out into the Gardens to see exciting examples from the plant collection. Pair this class with a tour of the Duke Research Greenhouse's teaching collection on Saturday, November 21 (register separately).
Source: Duke University, Sarah P. Duke Gardens

item.title: Tar Heel Preparedness Festival — Tue Sep 15, 11:00 AM — The Pit

Unleash your superhero, and join UNC Campus Safety for the Tar Heel Preparedness Festival on Tuesday, Sept. 15 from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. in the Pit and Polk Place. University departments, student organizations, and local, county, and state partners will share preparedness information, provide interactive activities, conduct live demonstrations, and help you discover the skills and resources needed to stay safe during an emergency.

item.title: OpenCourts Project - Biweekly Sync — Wed Sep 16, 7:30 PM
item.description:
Code with the Carolinas - Triangle Join volunteers at Code with the Carolinas for the biweekly meeting about OpenCourts, a project to build an open data portal for North and South Carolina legal data.. Starting with aggregate datasets from South Carolina courts, volunteers will be working to adopt this data (and our site being constructed to host it) to standards and measures more usable for accountability and analysis. These principles of analysis are drawn from guidance provided by the legal accountability organization [Measures for Justice](https://measuresforjustice.org/), whose limited work in the Carolinas we are trying to renew and expand.
This effort is building toward multi-state data portal that catalogues and publishes trusted, permissively-licensed court records to ensure open legal data remains a **public good** accessible to everyone. ️

item.title: The 1776 North Carolina Constitution — Wed Sep 23, 5:00 PM — Wilson Library
item.description:
North Carolina’s 1776 Constitution grew out of two crises: an east-west power struggle that erupted into the War of the Regulation, and a fight for political representation against an increasingly hostile English government. This lecture traces that story back to the religious and political conflicts of 17th-century Britain, through the migrations and economic pressures that shaped colonial North Carolina, to the document that remains the state’s constitutional foundation today.
The lecture is presented by an interdisciplinary team from Carolina Law, the History Department and the University Libraries.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Narrative of a Slave Woman: Songs of Hope, Justice, and Freedom — Fri Oct 23, 7:30 PM — Hill Hall
item.description:
FEATURING
LaToya Lain, soprano
PROGRAM
A powerful presentation by soprano LaToya Lain that examines the issue of slavery by combining musical performance with spoken narrative accounts. About the project, Lain says, “In 2003, HBO presented a documentary entitled ‘Unchained Memories’ about the stories of former slaves interviewed during the 1930s’ Federal Writers’ Project. As I read the print version of these slave narratives and later watched the documentary, I began to see how the stories of these men and women are told through the Negro Spirituals. I saw the direct relationship of some of my favorite spirituals and the life stories of remarkable slave women, whose names, if not for these narratives, we would have never known. I was inspired to take these narratives and combine them with concert arranged Negro Spirituals to tell the story of one former slave woman through song.”
PARKING

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Wed Nov 25, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: You Are Here Exhibition — Wed Nov 25, 10:00 AM — Witherspoon Student Center
item.description:
Join the African American Cultural Center to experience ariana Farquharson's You Are Here: Geolocating the Self through the Familiar in the Midst of the Unfamiliar. The exhibition is a speculative, immersive world-building study that invites guests to explore (geo)locating self and home amid a rapidly and frequently changing post-pandemic “new” world. It will be on display in the art gallery at the African American Cultural Center from Oct. 28, 2026, to Feb. 28, 2027. A behind-the-scenes look at the exhibition is set for Nov. 11.
Source: NC State African American Cultural Center
